groups.title: Tablet (273900ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for indigestion, loss of appetite, overeating, feeling stuffed, promotion of digestion, and a feeling of fullness in the stomach caused by indigestion.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 tablets per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution, or if you are pregnant or may be pregnant.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking another medicine.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E58700ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for pain relief in headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruise pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, period pain and pain from injury, and for reducing fever with chills.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 to 2 capsules per dose, 1 to 3 times in 1 day. Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose, 1 to 3 times in 1 day. Avoid taking it on an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut; if you have had an allergic reaction to soybean oil; if you have had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you are 30 weeks or more pregnant.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergy caused by a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if the user is a baby or young child aged 3 months or older and under 2 years of age; if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have lost a lot of fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea, are not taking in fluid or are taking a diuretic; if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; or if you are at particular risk from fat overload.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Do not take it continuously for a long period.

Do not take it together with another antipyretic analgesic, a cold medicine or a sedative.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, stomach discomfort, dizziness or swelling occurs, or if, rarely, anaphylactic shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters), asthma, very rarely erythema multiforme or exfoliative dermatitis, or a photosensitivity reaction, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis of unknown frequency occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (268600ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough and phlegm.
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you are breast-feeding; if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age for whom it is really necessary.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Babies and young children aged 7 years or younger should be given the syrup form. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take another antitussive-expectorant, a cold medicine, an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine) or a sedative. Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

If rash, reddening of the skin, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-coated Tablet (308000ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of inflammatory swelling after surgery and injury and in milk stasis (retained breast milk).
groups.usage: Adults: on the first day take 2 tablets per dose, 4 times in 1 day; after that, as a maintenance dose, take 1 tablet in 1 day, 4 times in 1 day. Much about how it works in the body is still not explained and the relationship between dose and effect has not been established, so do not take it without a clear purpose.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Do not take this medicine if you have a blood clotting disorder, severe liver or kidney impairment, if you are being given an anticoagulant, or if you are pregnant or may be pregnant.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

If rash, reddening of the skin, diarrhoea or constipation occurs, or occasionally loss of appetite, abdominal discomfort, nausea or vomiting, or rarely bleeding such as nosebleed or blood in the sputum occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (C30800ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical tiredness, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, during growth and in old age, for the relief of dryness of the eyes, for night blindness, for poor development of the bones and teeth, for the prevention of rickets, for the prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia, and for the supply of zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 8 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A in 1 day may cause birth defects. Women within the first 3 months of pregnancy and women who may be pregnant must not take it.

An overdose in a child aged 6 years or younger may cause death from iron poisoning, so keep it out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have high blood calcium (an excess of calcium in the blood); if you have sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause) or kidney disease; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have high blood potassium; if you have haemochromatosis (a disorder of iron metabolism in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas) or haemosiderosis; if you have anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency; if you have kidney stones; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hyperoxaluria (excessive excretion of oxalate in the urine); if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have gallbladder-related disease or liver disease; if you have acute or chronic bronchitis, pulmonary oedema, alkalosis or gout; if you have had kidney stones; if you are short of folic acid; or if you have a tendency to thrombosis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It may interfere with the detection of sugar in various urine tests, and it may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values.

Do not take it together with a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline preparation, an antacid or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, an antialdosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, loose stools, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, urticaria, a photosensitivity reaction, upper abdominal pain, cramps, fever, coma, allergic reactions, angioedema, joint pain, eosinophilia, iodine poisoning, high blood potassium, gas, gastrointestinal pain, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, pulmonary oedema, or menstruation coming earlier than expected, becoming heavier or bleeding for longer occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C, dry eyes, night blindness, poor bone and tooth development, prevention of rickets, iron deficiency anaemia and supply of zinc

groups.title: Soft Capsule (D22200ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose. Ages 7 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child aged 3 months or older and under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. Do not take it continuously for a long period. If symptoms do not improve after about 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) within the past 2 weeks. Consult a pharmacist if you have been given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes), cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever, or symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance and the like) occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or have had an allergic reaction to it.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or if, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing and the like), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body and on the mouth and eye membranes), asthma, liver function disorder (general lassitude, jaundice) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day, after a meal.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if the user is a premature baby or a young child.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It may interfere with the detection of sugar in various urine tests, and it may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with levodopa.

If nausea, vomiting, loose stools, diarrhoea, stomatitis, loss of appetite, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, constipation, erythema, urticaria, eczema, rash, maculopapular rash, itching, oedema, or oedema and fluid retention (in people with kidney failure or heart failure) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Ages 2 years to 6 years: take 5 mL as 1 dose. Ages 6 years to 12 years: take 10 mL as 1 dose. Take it every 4 to 6 hours, and do not take it 4 times or more within 24 hours.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.
